profile.reading:
This facility sits at 1301 West University Drive, Mesa, Arizona 85201; its OSM record labels it "PHX1 - Mesa," but Csquare's own current Phoenix-market page names the Mesa facility "PHX3," a separately owned, 50,256-square-foot building roughly 10 miles from Sky Harbor Airport, while Csquare's own "PHX1" code currently refers to a different, leased facility closer to downtown Phoenix. This profile flags that naming conflict explicitly rather than resolving it, since the "PHX1" label may reflect an older, pre-rebrand facility code (from Csquare's predecessor era as Cyxtera or Evoque) that has not propagated to third-party mapping data, while Csquare's current site uses "PHX3" for this Mesa address specifically. Csquare (formerly branded Centersquare, and before that a combination of Cyxtera, acquired out of Chapter 11 bankruptcy for $775 million in a deal completed January 2024, and Evoque, AT&T's divested data center business under Brookfield ownership since 2019) went public via IPO on NASDAQ in July 2026 at $21.00 per share. Csquare's SEC Form S-1 property table lists the Mesa asset as "Phoenix-PHX3_A," 49,827 square feet sellable, 67.2 percent leased as of March 31, 2026, closely matching the 50,256 square foot raised-floor figure on Csquare's public spec page; the building is Csquare-owned rather than leased. Csquare's Phoenix materials state 17.3 megawatts of utility power, 8 megawatts of UPS capacity, and 11.5 megawatts of generator capacity for this site, with SOC 1/2 Type II, PCI-DSS, NIST 800-53 PE High, and ISO 27001 compliance certifications. Csquare does not publish a year-opened date or name a power utility for this facility.

Mesa sits in the East Valley of the Phoenix metro, a submarket that has drawn substantial data center investment over the past decade given Arizona's dry climate, relatively low natural-disaster risk, and Arizona Public Service and Salt River Project utility infrastructure, alongside other operators including Vantage, EdgeConneX, and CyrusOne facilities in the broader region. Csquare's SEC S-1 discloses 389 megawatts of total sellable power capacity across its full 64-facility, 21-market portfolio as of March 31, 2026, and the same filing's Exhibit 2.1 confirms the October 31, 2023 Cyxtera asset purchase agreement between Cyxtera Technologies and Phoenix Data Center Holdings LLC, a Brookfield-affiliated acquisition vehicle whose name itself referenced the Phoenix market specifically.

sources.title: Csquare, Inc. Form S-1 Registration Statement

Facility specific seeding pass 2026-09-03, batch 95 (Centersquare): operator market page separates PHX1, Phoenix proper, from PHX3, Mesa, and this row city field favors a PHX3 match though the registry inherited name says PHX1, both figures recorded, no single capacity or sqft figure asserted as confirmed for this row, research_status upgraded from exhausted to complete, no address applied.

[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] This facility is attributed in the registry to Centersquare. This session found that centersquaredc.com, the legacy domain matching this registry entire Centersquare operator bucket naming, now issues a live redirect to www.csquare.com, the operator current domain, confirmed directly this session. Csquare own site states it owns and operates data centers built over decades by developing, acquiring, integrating, and operating advanced data centers, without giving a specific founding or rebrand date on the pages fetched this session. Csquare own site, fetched this session, lists corporate headquarters at 3100 Olympus Blvd, Suite 510, Coppell, TX 75019, and states a current portfolio of 80 total data centers, about 3.5 million square feet, more than 500 MW of power capacity, and more than 36,000 cross connects, across 15 North American markets plus London. On at least two Csquare pages fetched this session, a customer facing portal link pointed to evoquedcs.my.site.com, suggesting some relationship to Evoque Data Center Solutions, though this session found no page stating the exact nature of that relationship, such as whether Centersquare or Csquare is a direct rebrand of Evoque or a separate successor. Separately, this registry also carries an unrelated Cyxtera operator bucket, not part of this batch, already documented by an earlier pass in this registry as tracing to the same May 2017 CenturyLink data center divestiture discussed in this session own Lumen Technologies research, and as acquired by Cologix in 2023 per Cologix own site. This session found no evidence connecting that Cyxtera and Cologix history to the Centersquare, Csquare, or Evoque names researched for this batch, so the two threads are treated as distinct and unconfirmed to be related. This registry also carries a separate Csquare operator bucket, not part of this batch, whose name is now confirmed by the redirect evidence above to very likely be the same current brand as the Centersquare bucket this batch covers, though this session did not merge or rename either bucket, flagging this as an open duplicate operator naming question for a future dedicated pass rather than resolving it unilaterally. This row is named in the registry as Centersquare, Phoenix, PHX1, Mesa, with a city field of Mesa, AZ. The operator own current market page for Phoenix, fetched this session, treats PHX1 and PHX3 as two separate facilities, describing PHX1 as ten minutes from Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport and fifteen minutes from downtown Phoenix at 13.3 MW UPS capacity and 40,456 square feet of raised floor, and describing PHX3 as in Mesa, about ten miles from Phoenix Sky Harbor Airport, at 17.3 MW utility power, 8 MW UPS and 11.5 MW generator, and 50,256 square feet of raised floor. Because this row own city field says Mesa and the operator page places PHX3, not PHX1, in Mesa, this session leans toward PHX3 as the more consistent current match for this row, but the registry own inherited name still says PHX1, so this session records both operator published figures in this reading rather than asserting a single confirmed number, and flags the PHX1 versus PHX3 naming question for a future researcher rather than silently picking one.

reading.body:
This campus sits in Mesa, Arizona, on the Centersquare operator's published footprint. The operator lists two Phoenix-area facilities: PHX1 at 13.3 MW UPS capacity and 40,456 square feet of raised floor, and PHX3 in Mesa at 17.3 MW utility power, 8 MW UPS, 11.5 MW generator capacity, and 50,256 square feet of raised floor. The registry entry and operator's own market page differ on which facility sits at this address, so both figures appear here: if this is PHX1, the campus offers 13.3 MW; if PHX3, it offers 17.3 MW utility power plus 8 MW UPS.

Taking the larger figure of 17.3 MW utility power as a working assumption, this represents roughly 430 racks at 40 kW per rack, a common density for AI training clusters, or roughly 1,700 racks at 10 kW per rack, a density more typical of inference deployments. The operator's specifications do not publish IT load, customer mix, or utilization, so the actual mix of training, inference, or other workloads is not known. The facility's 11.5 MW generator and 8 MW UPS indicate capability to sustain operations during grid events for some fraction of its utility draw.

In Arizona's published capacity landscape, this campus ranks fifth among four facilities that have released power figures to the public, in a state with 56 mapped data center locations and 512 MW of total published capacity. The operator holds a current portfolio of over 500 MW across 80 facilities in 15 North American markets, so this single campus represents less than 4% of their stated capacity. Whether this facility matters to AI scaling depends on whether it is spoken for by existing tenants or available for new compute-intensive workloads, a question the published specifications do not answer.
